newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates lower on big banks lending.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates lower on big banks lending.

text.p: Interbank rates fell across the board on Wednesday due to lending by big banks, dealers said.
They said the banks could be lending on behalf of Bank Negara in a move to improve market liquidity.
Recent tightness particularly at the short-end of the market had kept rates firm.
"I think Bank Negara is injecting funds to help ease the market. Rates have not shown signs of coming off as liquidity remains tight," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said foreign banks, which had some excess funds, were among the lenders this morning.
Bidders were again mostly small banks and finance companies, they said.
One- and two-week money were at 7.80/8.30 percent against 8.50/60 percent on Tuesday.
One-month money was at 8.10/20 percent from 8.40/50, and three-month at 8.00/10 percent against 8.00/20.
The overnight rate, which closed at 8.30/40 percent on Tuesday, was expected to trade between 7.5 and 8.0 percent in line with the drop in interbank rates.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were up across the board, on the expectation of a softening in interest rates, futures dealers said.
At 0300 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was up four points to 92.02, or an implied yield of 7.98 percent.
September contract was up five at 92.36, or 7.64 percent, and December was up two at 92.47, or 7.53 percent,
